chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Ali ibn Al-Numan, raising it (to the Imam), said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), when he ascended Al-Safa, would face the Kaaba, then raise his hands, then say: 'O Allah, forgive me every sin that I have committed at any time. So if I return (to sinning), then return to me with forgiveness, for You are the Forgiving, the Merciful.'

O Allah, deal with me what You are worthy of, for if You deal with me what You are worthy of, You will show mercy to me; and if You punish me, then You are Self-Sufficient from my punishment, and I am in need of Your mercy. So, O He to Whose mercy I am in need, have mercy on me.

O Allah, do not deal with me what I am worthy of, for if You deal with me what I am worthy of, You will punish me, and You will not be oppressing me. I have come to fear Your justice, and I do not fear Your injustice, so O He Who is Just and does not act unjustly, have mercy on me.

key_terms.الصَّفَا: Al-Safa (one of the hills in Mecca)

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication of Imam Ali (AS) when ascending Al-Safa?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi highlights the specific supplication (Dua) of Imam Ali (AS) during the Sa'i between Safa and Marwa, reflecting the Shia tradition of emulating the Imams' ritual practices. The supplication masterfully balances the concepts of divine justice (Adl) and mercy (Rahma), acknowledging that while humans deserve punishment for sins, God’s inherent generosity warrants forgiveness. It serves as a model for pilgrims to combine humility with confidence in God's boundless compassion.
